queue_dispositions.authoritative_rule_set: Screen Australia's current list contains 12 treaty partners and two MOU partners. Official status requires an applicable arrangement, independent co-producers, matching financial and creative participation, nationality/personnel and territorial compliance, provisional applications before pre-production, and joint competent-authority approval. Arrangement-specific format rules control. Official status treats the work as Australian and can bypass the Significant Australian Content test for Producer Offset eligibility, but neither certification nor funding is automatic.

queue_dispositions.authoritative_rule_set: Telefilm's current official directory displays 57 country/territory headings, with the Belgium heading covering the Flemish, French and German-speaking Communities; Canadian Heritage reports 59 partner countries. Each pathway is governed by its own treaty/MOU. Telefilm requires a Canadian-controlled production company, preliminary recommendation normally at least 30 days before shooting (60 days for Hungary, Poland, Switzerland or Hong Kong), joint authority recognition, and arrangement-specific financial, creative, technical, nationality, format and territorial compliance. Contributions range from 15%-30% under the applicable treaty; participation and expenditure must be proportional. Treaty status gives national status, but CPTC and other incentives require separate applications and their remaining requirements.
